investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent from the check result.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning from starting. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval-runner code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be asserted without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only the two peerpods nodes via affinity/selector rules, and those rules may be overly restrictive or may have drifted from the actual node labels in the cluster, reducing the schedulable pool to exactly the two already-saturated nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of peerpods-capable nodes (2 of 6) may be insufficient for the current eval and workload concurrency, and no autoscaling or preemption policy is configured to recover.

Lower confidence — transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run temporarily exhausted VM slots; slots may self-recover once existing agents are cleaned up.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T08:38–08:43Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the eval probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) never produced a running VM, the check terminated before it could collect any evidence, leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any new remote-agent pod on the production cluster at the time of the eval run. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots, and the other four nodes were excluded by node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144 s before the eval timed out, so createAgent never returned a valid agent, and the probe produced zero evidence against the contract's four required fields (expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata peer-pod nodes were consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval probe's pod.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy, so the effective scheduling pool is already limited to those 2 nodes, amplifying any capacity pressure.

[Medium confidence] Concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked eval pods consuming remaining VM slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not release their kata VMs, the resource pool could be depleted at eval time.

[Low confidence] Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster may be insufficient for the expected concurrent load, requiring node scaling or additional kata-capable nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning from starting. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval-runner code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for a pod stuck 144s, confirming the condition persisted across sequential eval attempts.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for a pod stuck 147s, confirming the condition persisted a third time.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent because the pod never reached a running state and no VM was provisioned.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=135818, endedAt=2026-07-09T08:38:37.451Z — the eval timed out waiting for pod scheduling, not during agent logic.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be asserted without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets only the two peerpods nodes via affinity/selector rules, and those rules may be overly restrictive or may have drifted from the actual node labels in the cluster, reducing the schedulable pool to exactly the two already-saturated nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of peerpods-capable nodes (2 of 6) may be insufficient for the current eval and workload concurrency, and no autoscaling or preemption policy is configured to recover.

Lower confidence — transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run temporarily exhausted VM slots; slots may self-recover once existing agents are cleaned up.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any new remote-agent pod on the production cluster at the time of the eval run.
